stem: A group of learners are given a Venn diagram of the sample space $S=\{n:n\in\mathbb{Z},1\leq n\leq {=nn}\}$. The diagram has two overlapping circles, one for event set $A$ and one for event set $B$. The numbers written inside circle $A$ are {=ash[0]}, {=ash[1]}, {=ash[2]}, {=ash[3]}, {=ash[4]} and {=ash[5]}. The numbers written inside circle $B$ are {=bsh[0]}, {=bsh[1]} and {=bsh[2]}. A number in the overlap of the two circles is inside both circles, so it is written in both lists, and every other number of $S$ lies outside both circles. The learners are asked to identify the event set of the intersection of $A$ and $B$, also written $A\cap B$. Which set best describes the event set of $A\cap B$?
solution: The intersection $A\cap B$ is the set of numbers that are in circle $A$ and in circle $B$ at the same time. It can only contain numbers that are written inside circle $B$ as well as inside circle $A$.

Check the numbers of circle $B$, which are {=bset[0]}, {=bset[1]} and {=bset[2]}, against circle $A$. The numbers {=inter[0]} and {=inter[1]} are inside circle $A$ too, but {=bonly} is only in circle $B$, so it is left out.
Write down only the numbers that are in both circles: $A\cap B=\{{=inter[0]}, {=inter[1]}\}$.

The other sets are not the intersection: $\{{=bset[0]}, {=bset[1]}, {=bset[2]}\}$ is the whole of $B$, $\{{=aset[0]}, {=aset[1]}, {=aset[2]}, {=aset[3]}, {=aset[4]}, {=aset[5]}\}$ is the whole of $A$, and $\{{=uset[0]}, {=uset[1]}, {=uset[2]}, {=uset[3]}, {=uset[4]}, {=uset[5]}, {=uset[6]}\}$ collects the numbers of both circles. The intersection keeps only the shared numbers.
notes: Models the book question ex14-4-1 (p. 482). I read its figure: the book draws two overlapping circles with A holding many numbers, B holding {7, 10, 11}, the overlap {7, 10} and one number (8) outside both. Stems carry no figure, so the Venn diagram is described in words: each circle's contents are listed, an overlap number appears in both lists (the stem says so), and the numbers of S that are in neither circle are not listed. Each instance has A with 6 numbers, B with 3 and exactly 2 shared, like the book's 2-element answer. The lists are shuffled so the shared numbers do not sit in the same position every time. Distractors are the book's own error types: all of B (whole-set), all of A (whole-set), and the union of both circles (either-set). Sizes 2, 3, 6 and 7 make the four options always distinct. Reviewer check: pool entries 0-1 are shared, 2-5 are in A only, 6 is in B only, so A and B overlap in exactly the two numbers shown as the key.
